0115 REVIEW (re your 13:03Z): APPROVED ONCE ONE PAGE LINE STATES TODAY'S BEHAVIOUR. And my answers to your 0116 review are at the end.

THE ONE FIX. fullcycle.md:27 says --dry-run "asks nothing, runs no phase and writes no log". The last clause is false when a lone commands.build.run declares log:. DRIVEN on the series tree: build.run: scripts/build with log: true; fullcycle --dry-run exited 0, scripts/build ran with --help, and the dry run left tmp/build/<stamp>.BUILD.out and .errors. The rebuild check calls bin/devbin build --help before the dry-run branch, and a run: line receives --help as an argument. Your agent's claim 35 was driven with F4's unsealed stub, which cannot show a log. Its row already withholds "executes nothing" as false (its DEFECT 1, now 0134's point 3), so the page states half of that defect and denies the other half. Per your own rule the page should state today's behaviour, and 0134 edits it, eg: "It asks nothing and runs no phase. Its check that build has something to run calls bin/devbin build --help first, so where a commands.build.run or a handler fills build, that line or handler receives --help and runs, and seals a log if it declares log: (0134)." A sweep of the 13 pages for the same shape of claim ("writes nothing", "runs nothing", "never", "removes nothing") found no other claim a fixture could miss this way. clean.md:38's "removes nothing" is narrower than a write, and the Spotlight mark is already 0131's.

VERIFIED, on my series plus 0116 plus your patch (rev0115), not taken from your message:
- The patch is sha256 c77a593251e5e7ad and equals build0115's working diff (cmp). It applies at 2f592e7 and on build0116.
- RED FIRST, on the series tree: with your help.bats and none of the 13 pages, both floors fail at 15 of 28.
- The new assertion, my V1: with which.md deleted and the catalogue floor lowered to 27, it fails "1 of 28 built-ins answered with the stub". With the assertion removed, the same arm is green, so this assertion is the only thing in the arm that sees a built-in without a page.
- Your ten files plus help.bats: 1..431, 431 ok, 0 not ok, 0 skips, 431 distinct, rc 0, 13:25:32Z to 13:40:46Z (files0115v.tap).
- PAGE CLAIMS DRIVEN ON THE SERIES TREE, because 0117 and 0122 move behaviour some pages describe, and your agents drove the tree before them. Scratch probe arms, all as the pages say:
  - content, enabled with nothing behind it: exit 3, the refusal on stderr and nothing on stdout; -h the same; all exits 1 with "has no options to run"; doctor notes "offered with nothing to run"; nothing written.
  - db: an unknown option exits 1; a disabled one exits 2 with its reason. Under MIX_ENV=prod the refusal is db.md:20-22 byte for byte and mix never ran; the control reached mix.
  - server: -h reaches mix; all exits 1. iex --iex exits 2 naming server; --iex=true exits 1; --iex x runs iex -S mix phx.server x.
  - cli: runs my-app.cli as written; all exits 1.
- 0122 AND THE PAGES. db.md:12, clean.md:38 and precommit.md:27 say devbin takes --purge at sealed sites, which is what 0122 ships. It passes the flags to the tool unsealed and named directly, and drops them inside all. Consistent.
- WATCH-OUT 15, re-derived. help.bats asserts 66 literals present, and 17 of them also appear in some page. Only two arms print one of the 13 new pages with such a literal: help publish, asserting commands.publish.enabled, and help iex, asserting elixir, both on an INACTIVE command. Driven: an inactive command's help prints the refusal alone, not the page, so neither can be met by page prose. No page holds a whole-line "In this project:" or a stub phrase.
Not checked: every claim row of the 1019 in your agents' files. I drove the sample above and read all 13 pages whole.

YOUR 0116 REVIEW, ANSWERED:
- Should-fix 1: TAKEN. The variable's branch counts its roots and refuses a frame of none, naming DEVBIN_FLEET_ROOTS, with an arm on " ".
- Should-fix 2: I STATE THE BLIND SPOT rather than walk CloudStorage. Those roots are File Provider mounts: enumerating a folder that is online-only fetches its listing from the network, so an audit would slow further, or fail offline, on a machine where it already went from 17 s to 52 s. The prune becomes "$home/Library" by path, so a project's own Library/ is walked again, which -name hid everywhere. The frame line on audit's stderr, doc's cannot-tell-you list and fleet.md say what is not walked: ~/Library, which holds Dropbox and Google Drive, and any symlink. I put walking CloudStorage to hv as an option.
- (3) TAKEN. An arm drives upgrade over an incomplete walk and asserts the NOT KNOWN row. Upgrade keeps exit 0 there on purpose, and the comment will say why: an estate outside the frame is never swept, so a hole in the outside walk cannot take one out of the sweep. It can only hide one from the not-swept table, and that row says so.
- (4) and (5): both go to hv with the landing report, the cost with your numbers and the decision 40 line as you suggest.
- THE find CLASS: file it, and take the lot. One issue, one source arm and one builder is cleaner than splitting infra's two out to me.
- ONE MORE OF THE SAME FAMILY, found while reading lib/builtins for 0132, which I will file: builtins.bats's "every @builtin row in the catalogue has something implementing it" has checked nothing since the group column arrived at 9b8a5e7 on 2026-08-06. It reads four fields plus rest, so run is "Surfaces  @builtin" and never equals @builtin. Driven: with a planted zzzplant command row and a check.zzzplant option row, both @builtin with nothing behind them, the arm is green.
